newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel economic officials extend talks to Monday.
newsitem.headline: Israel economic officials extend talks to Monday.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel will continue talks on the government budget deficit on Monday, the Treasury said on Sunday night.
It said that at the start of the meeting on Sunday evening no recommendations were made concerning the budget deficit and only treasury officials had the opportunity to speak.

A source present at the meeting quoted treasury officials saying the government's domestic budget deficit in first quarter 1997 totalled 503 million shekels. The treasury had forecast that the budget would be balanced in the first quarter.
The officials said that this size deficit in the first quarter would translate into a one billion shekel deficit in annual terms.
The source quoted Meridor as forecasting economic growth of only three percent this year. Meridor blamed most of the slowdown on the Bank of Israel's tight monetary policy.
The central bank has urged the government to cut the 1997 budget to keep the deficit within the target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Pessimists among analysts say the government will miss the target by 0.8 percent of GDP or three to four billion shekels.
Beside the domestic deficit, the government had a foreign deficit of 700 million shekels in the first quarter.
